prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D geometry of a 3 to 4 metre wide checkpoint lane flanked by raised curbs, showing the camera wearer's motorcycle handlebars, mirrors, and dashboard brightest in the lower foreground at 0.5 to 0.8 metres (within arm's reach) while the ground plane darkens smoothly with distance ahead. Across the five frames, the camera wearer advances rapidly forward so that the left-side hedge (1.5 to 3 metres to the left in frames 1 and 2), vertical pillar, three planter boxes, right-side red barrier with traffic cones (2 to 6 metres away in frame 3), and the left guard booth (4 to 5 metres away from the right-side booth across the lane) brighten as they move from roughly 20 to 30 metres ahead in frame 1 to 1.5 to 4 metres alongside the rider before exiting the left and right edges of the view. No other people are present in the scene, and the camera wearer faces straight ahead down the lane with their torso and lower motorcycle occluded below the bottom frame edge. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map more clearly separates the foreground vertical pillar, stepped curb edges, and individual planter boxes from the brightly lit background booth in frame 3, and highlights the thin vertical barrier post on the right in frames 4 and 5 (~4 to 6 metres ahead) against the dark night sky. However, the map is unreliable on the overarching canopy roof above, which is lost in black background values despite being overhead, and on the thin horizontal boom barrier arm ahead (~6 to 10 metres away in frame 5), which completely vanishes into the dark far-field.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a few discrete foreground and mid-ground regions against an unlabelled black background while missing most of the checkpoint scene, where no other people are present and the camera wearer faces forward along the lane. In the bottom foreground within arm's reach (0.5 to 0.8 metres below and in front of the camera wearer), it outlines the visible top portion of the motorcycle handlebars and mirrors while the rest of the vehicle and the rider's body remain out of view below the frame. In frame 3, it segments three roadside planter boxes on the left curb (roughly 2.5 to 5 metres ahead and 0.5 to 1 metre apart from each other) as 'potted plant' and the left guard booth behind them (5 to 8 metres away) as 'microwave', before labelling the approaching booth at 2 to 4 metres on the upper left in frame 4 and the raised yellow-and-black median curb at 1.5 to 5 metres on the right in frames 4 and 5 as 'train'. While the masks help delineate the exact footprints of the three individual planter boxes in frame 3 and the inner median island in frames 4 and 5 as they pass from ahead to alongside the rider, the semantic class labels are highly unreliable throughout. Specifically, the foreground handlebars and rider hands switch classes from 'motorcycle' in frames 1 and 2 to 'person' in frames 3 through 5, the building and curb are misclassified as 'microwave' and 'train', and critical obstacles such as the right-side red barrier and cones in frames 1 to 3 and the horizontal boom gate 6 to 10 metres ahead in frames 4 and 5 are omitted entirely.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely black across all five frames, confirming the absence of any other people standing or walking in the checkpoint lane or inside the flanking booths. Only the camera wearer is present, facing forward down the lane with both hands gripping the motorcycle handlebars within arm's reach at roughly 0.5 to 0.7 metres below and in front of the camera, while the rest of the wearer's body is out of view below the bottom edge of the frame. Across the five frames, the pose detector fails to render any magenta hand skeletons for the camera wearer's visible hands on the left and right grips, producing only a single spurious yellow body-keypoint cluster on the lower-left handlebar mirror and left hand in frame 2 (about 0.6 metres from the camera). Nothing is revealed by this map that is hard to see in the RGB strip alone, as the rider's hands on the controls are clearly visible in RGB. The map is highly unreliable for egocentric hand tracking here, missing both hands in every frame and hallucinating a partial body skeleton on the motorcycle hardware in frame 2.
